_readme: Creator Marketing and Partnerships, Version 1.0: the page's words and its media configuration, section by section (src/pages/work/creator-campaigns.astro and src/components/creator/). Copy follows John's Creator Marketing and Partnerships V1.0 brief (October 17, 2026): the approved hero paragraph word for word, the V1 placeholder headline he supplied, his working headlines for the program context and the program ownership, and his confirmed creator roster (eight creators, their affiliations and destinations exactly as given). The per-destination creator counts follow that roster (6, 7 and 4, which make the 17 participations), and the content counts, the trip types and the co-sponsors come from the case study's earlier approved copy. A field set to null is a V1 placeholder: it shows as a labeled placeholder in `npm run dev` only and renders nothing in a production build, so the public page never shows one (testimonials, Trezor's assignment, objective, approach, metrics and collaboration credits, the creators' category labels, the Mykonos sponsor identifiers, and the editing and filming credits). Media slots name asset ids in src/data/assets.json; every slot already holds its final aspect ratio, all of them square or landscape.

hero._hero: 05 Hero: one full-screen landscape composition in layers (the coastal-estate reference, used for the hero only): the sky, the headline, the villa and its palms in front of the headline's lower line, and two palm fronds at the corners, each moving at its own rate as the page scrolls, with a slow drift of their own; reduced motion holds the layers still. The photographs are illustrative stock (Unsplash), credited in the hero and in the credits, and never presented as footage from the trips.
hero.label: 01 / Creator Marketing and Partnerships
hero.headline: Bringing creator campaigns to life around the world.
hero.copy: I developed and managed creator programs that brought brands, talent, and memorable settings together across Costa Rica, Singapore, and Mykonos, connecting partnership strategy with production, distribution, and measurable campaign outcomes.
hero.credit: Illustrative photography: Rosemary Media and Abbie Bernet, Unsplash

context._context: 06 Program context: John's working headline, one concise paragraph that establishes his responsibilities in prose (no services grid), and a single drawn route that leaves the paragraph and leads into the creator network.
context.headline: The trip was the setting. The program connected everything around it.
context.accent: The program connected everything around it.
context.copy: For Bolt Liquidity, each trip put creators, sponsors, and a production plan in one place for a few days. Around it, I ran the program: finding the creators and keeping those relationships, coordinating sponsors, setting the campaign strategy, planning the trip and its production, briefing and approving the work, running the shoot on location, and carrying it through distribution and reporting.

network._network: 07 Creator network: exactly the eight creators John confirmed, square profile pictures traveling one way, slowly, around a curved path in depth (the reference recording's depth on the custom-spaces curve), with no controls and nothing to drag. Hovering, focusing or selecting a creator shows their name, affiliations and destinations at the center; nothing on the cards is a testimonial, a follower count or a ranking. Reduced motion holds the ring still; narrow screens show a plain list with everything visible. `category` is a V1 placeholder label (null until John confirms one).
network.headline: The creators who made it travel.
network.sub: Eight creators across 17 participations in Costa Rica, Singapore, and Mykonos.

creators.name: The Blonde Broker
affiliations: VP of Financial Services at Corgi

voices._voices: 08 The testimonial transition: up to three short creator testimonials (one or two sentences each), one at a time as the page scrolls, lower left, lower right, then lower left again on the way into the destinations, each with its attribution. They are V1 placeholders (assets.json, pending): until one is approved the section renders nothing in a production build and the network leads straight into the atlas. Never on the creator cards, and never Trezor's feedback, which belongs to the Trezor section.

atlas._atlas: 09 Campaign atlas: one stage that holds still while the reader scrolls through three states, Costa Rica, Singapore and Mykonos, each with its own loop (5 to 10 seconds, silent, landscape, reset with a dissolve), two fragments, color atmosphere, large name, chapter index and concise copy. Wide screens with motion allowed pin it; narrow or short screens, reduced motion and no JavaScript show the three chapters one after another. Counts: creators from the confirmed roster, content pieces from the earlier approved copy. `sponsors` names logo ids in src/data/logos.json; null is a V1 placeholder.
atlas.title: Three destinations, one program.

destinations.name: Costa Rica
destinations.copy: A creator house on the Pacific coast. Pool days and golden-hour beaches set the scene, and sponsor integrations were built into what the creators were already filming.

destinations.name: Singapore
destinations.copy: A crypto game show on a moving party bus, high tea on the 56th floor, and a shopping spree through the city's luxury malls, run as a conference activation.

destinations.name: Mykonos
destinations.copy: A villa above the Aegean, a day on a catamaran, and long dinners into the evening, with four creators turning each moment into content.

trezor._trezor: 10 The Trezor campaign: the final video first (Trezor Dare Ad.mp4, with sound, on request), then the assignment, the objective, the approach, the exact metrics, Trezor's feedback (one concise attributed quote, kept apart from the creator testimonials) and the collaboration credits, revealed in that order as the reader scrolls. Assignment, objective, approach, metrics and the creator, production and editing credits are V1 placeholders until John supplies them; no vague metric is ever stated.
trezor.title: The Trezor dare
trezor.deck: A creator-led sponsor integration for Trezor, filmed at the creator house in Costa Rica.

montage._montage: 11 Selected content: one curated, silent montage (cm-montage.mp4, a dissolve at its reset) from across the three trips, landscape only and smaller than the Trezor film, with the formats listed beside it and the one on screen marked as it plays. `at` is the loop time in seconds where each excerpt takes over (the middle of the dissolve into it).
montage.headline: One program, many formats.
montage.copy: A short cut from across the three trips, from destination films and creator ads to the game show, sponsor integrations, social clips, and the crew at work behind them.

ownership._ownership: 12 Program ownership: John's working headline, its first sentence above a waterline and its second below it, where the areas he ran sit as one typographic field rather than a grid, timeline or checklist.
ownership.headline: The experience was visible. The system behind it was not.
ownership.below: The system behind it was not.
ownership.copy: Beneath every post sat the work I ran, from the first creator conversation to the final partner report.

credits._credits: 13 Credits: one system for every contributor, set like a film's closing credits. John's rows name strategy, program management, direction and coordination; editing, filming and design are credited to the people who did them, and nothing implies John edited, shot or designed the work. Rows whose names are null are V1 placeholders.
credits.title: Many hands, one program.

rows.names: Eva, The Blonde Broker, Ashley, Shiv, Raj, Arcanic, Caleb, and Simon
Bolt Liquidity's design, editing, and legal teams
Rosemary Media and Abbie Bernet, Unsplash (illustrative, not from the trips)

credits.note: Creators performed and published the campaign content, and internal designers and editors completed final builds and edits where applicable. My part was the strategy, the program management, and the direction and coordination of production.

conclusion._conclusion: 14 The conclusion: one short idea (a connected program produced content right away and value that lasted), then the way on to the next case study in order (Technical Product Marketing), then the shared Contact section.
conclusion.headline: Every trip paid off twice.
conclusion.copy: Because sourcing, sponsorship, production, and distribution ran as one connected program, each trip delivered a wave of content right away, then left relationships with creators and partners that kept creating value long after.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I turn technical complexity into a clear market narrative.
